newsitem.title: TURKEY: SOCCER SHOWCASE-FENERBAHCE AND GALATASARAY SEEK FORM OF OLD.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-FENERBAHCE AND GALATASARAY SEEK FORM OF OLD.

text.p: Fenerbahce and Galatasaray will be praying for a return to the form of the first half of the season when the two leading teams in Turkey meet in a crucial match on Sunday.

Both clubs enter the fray in dismal form, neither of them having won since the season moved into its second phase. Fenerbahce, beaten last week by lowly Altay, have scored just two goals in league matches and Galatasaray one.

"We lost six points by drawing the three matches of the second half. It is now time to make up for those losses," said Galatasaray deputy chairman Ergun Gursoy after their draw last week against an in-form Kocaelispor.

That mood of frustration, which saw elements of the crowd booing and throwing plastic bottles at the players, has done nothing to relieve the pressure and nor has coach Fatih Terim's ultimatum to his team.
"If you continue to play like this, you will come home under police escort. If you start playing like before, you will return on your fans' shoulders -- the choice is yours," he told them.

The main cause for concern is the goal drought being suffered by their leading marksmanl Hakan Sukur. He was last on target in the week before the mid-season break when he collected a hat-trick against Bursaspor.
With Arif Erdem, just back from military service, also struggling to find the net, the creativity and workrate of Romanian playmaker Gheorghe Hagi has largely gone to waste.
Fortunately for Galatasaray, their poor form has been matched by their rivals and they remain top of the first division with 47 points, three clear of Fenerbahce.
Fenerbahce look the likely winners, given their impressive home record and they will doubtless enjoy a psychological advantage after their 4-0 trouncing of Galatasaray in October.

But their preparation has been upset by growing speculation over the future of their Brazilian coach Sebastiao Lazaroni. Having seen his side dumped out of the Turkish Cup by Besiktas on Wednesday, he faces the sack if they fail to win on Sunday.

Lazaroni has been criticised for altering the side left by his predecessor, fellow Brazilian Alberto Parreira, who guided Fenerbahce to European Champions' League qualification and a historic win over Manchester United at Old Trafford last year.
He has been attacked for playing men out of position and upsetting the rhythm while his persistent exclusion of Bulgarian Emil Kostadinov has also raised eyebrows.

Reports that the team almost missed a plane back to Istanbul because he was berating his players for such a long time after their defeat at Altay, suggest that the pressure is getting to the Brazilian.

Their task will not be made any easier by the likely absence of Turkey's top goalkeeper Rustu Recber, who is doing military service, and the poor form of Nigerian striker Augustine Okocha, who has been complaining of exhaustion.

The management has responded by treating the build-up to Sunday's game as if it were a cup final. The players will not be allowed to leave their training camp until they travel to ground for Sunday's match.
"Fenerbahce spent billions of lira on their team at the beginning of the season. And we will make sure we see the results of this," club deputy chairman Vefa Kucuk said.
"This week, with a win against Fenerbahce, we will earn three points and consolidate our lead."
